title: Phoenix Wright: Ace Attorney – Spirit of Justice
subtitle: A courtroom governed by the dead
summary: Phoenix Wright: Ace Attorney – Spirit of Justice is Capcom's Nintendo 3DS legal adventure dividing its cases between the Wright Anything Agency and the kingdom of Khura'in. Phoenix travels to meet Maya Fey and encounters a justice system that relies on a victim's final experiences. Apollo and Athena continue the agency's work elsewhere, connecting the two settings through a returning defence team. The unfamiliar courtroom gives Phoenix a different kind of testimony to challenge, while the wider story follows the consequences of trying to defend someone within that system.
body: Phoenix Wright: Ace Attorney – Spirit of Justice is Capcom's Nintendo 3DS legal adventure dividing its cases between the Wright Anything Agency and the kingdom of Khura'in. Phoenix travels to meet Maya Fey and encounters a justice system that relies on a victim's final experiences. Apollo and Athena continue the agency's work elsewhere, connecting the two settings through a returning defence team. The unfamiliar courtroom gives Phoenix a different kind of testimony to challenge, while the wider story follows the consequences of trying to defend someone within that system.

Khura'in's Divination Séance presents the victim's last sensations as a vision accompanied by the priestess's explanation. The player examines what is seen and perceived, then identifies where that material contradicts the interpretation offered to the court. A supernatural source therefore becomes something that still needs careful reading. The sequence adds another form of evidence to the series' hearings. An apparently decisive account can contain a misleading assumption, and the defence makes progress by separating the experience itself from what somebody claims it proves about the crime.

Outside the Khura'in hearings, the returning lawyers retain their distinctive investigative techniques. Phoenix can confront hidden secrets through Psyche-Locks, Apollo notices revealing habits, and Athena examines conflicting emotions with the Mood Matrix. Investigations also allow three-dimensional scenes to be viewed from different perspectives while gathering evidence. These tools create different ways of approaching a reluctant witness or an incomplete account. The cases continue to depend on the same basic work of understanding the record, but the available methods change with the lawyer and the place in which the hearing unfolds.
story_headings: A courtroom governed by the dead
A vision still needs an interpretation
